🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A Florida mother was arrested at Orlando International Airport after authorities say she left her four children, ages 9 to 14, home without overnight adult supervision while she traveled to Las Vegas for work.

Irene Miller, 50, of Kissimmee, was arrested on October 23 as she arrived back in Florida, according to the Osceola County Sheriff's Office. She faces four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm, one count for each child, authorities said.

The case began on the night of October 21, when one of the children called 911 to report that a dumbbell had fallen on her 9-year-old brother's head, the sheriff's office said. Deputies who responded to the family's Kissimmee home found the four children there with no adult present. Fire rescue crews took the injured boy to Celebration Hospital, where he was treated and released.

Deputies reached Miller by phone and learned she had left Florida on October 18 for a work trip to Las Vegas and planned to return October 23, authorities said. Miller told deputies she had arranged for a babysitter to travel from Tampa each morning to help the children get ready for school and check on them after school, but the babysitter was not required to stay overnight, according to the sheriff's office.

The children's father was contacted and agreed to take all four children to his home, authorities said. Detectives then arranged to meet Miller when her flight landed at Orlando International Airport on October 23, and she was taken into custody there.

"The Osceola County Sheriff's Office will not tolerate child neglect. These cases will be investigated, and charges will be brought against the parents who are not properly supervising or caring for their children," Sheriff Chris Blackmon said in a statement.

The charges against Miller are allegations, and she is presumed innocent until proven guilty. No plea had been publicly reported as of Tuesday, October 27.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post; USA TODAY; Osceola County Sheriff's Office.
